explanations.name: TileStructure.Forest.adjoint_tile_support1
explanations.statement: Let $X$ be a metric space carrying the doubling measure and function-distance structure of the tile structure, let $a\in\mathbb{N}$, $q\in\mathbb{R}$, let $K:X\to X\to\mathbb{C}$, $\sigma_1,\sigma_2:X\to\mathbb{Z}$ and bounded measurable sets $F,G\subseteq X$ be the data of the proof (`ProofData a q K σ₁ σ₂ F G`), and let $\mathfrak{P}X$ be the tile structure with parameters $Q$, grid constant $D=2^{\mathbb{c}a^2}$ (`defaultD a`, $\mathbb{c}$ a fixed numerical constant), $\kappa=2^{-10a}$ (`defaultκ a`), $S$ (`defaultS X`) and base point `cancelPt X`. For a tile $p\in\mathfrak{P}X$ write $\mathfrak{I}(p)$ for its dyadic cube (with centre $\mathfrak{c}(p)$ and integer scale $\mathfrak{s}(p)$), $E(p)=\{y\in\mathfrak{I}(p): Q(y)\in\Omega(p),\ \sigma_1(y)\le\mathfrak{s}(p)\le\sigma_2(y)\}$, $K_s(x,y)=K(x,y)\,\psi(D^{-s}\operatorname{dist}(x,y))$ for the cutoff $\psi$ used in `Ks`, and $T_p^*f(x)=\int_{E(p)}\overline{K_{\mathfrak{s}(p)}(y,x)}\,e^{i(Q(y)(y)-Q(y)(x))}f(y)\,dy$. Then for every $f:X\to\mathbb{C}$ the adjoint Carleson operator is supported in the ball of radius $5D^{\mathfrak{s}(p)}$ around $\mathfrak{c}(p)$ and only sees $f$ on $\mathfrak{I}(p)$: $$T_p^*f=\mathbf{1}_{B(\mathfrak{c}(p),\,5D^{\mathfrak{s}(p)})}\cdot T_p^*\bigl(\mathbf{1}_{\mathfrak{I}(p)}f\bigr).$$
explanations.summary: The proof shows that the adjoint Carleson operator of a tile $p$ is insensitive to $f$ off the cube $\mathfrak{I}(p)$ — because it integrates only over $E(p)\subseteq\mathfrak{I}(p)$ — and is supported in the ball $B(\mathfrak{c}(p),5D^{\mathfrak{s}(p)})$. The first fact is the lemma `adjoint_eq_adjoint_indicator`; for the second, one works pointwise: where $T_p^*(\mathbf{1}_{\mathfrak{I}(p)}f)$ vanishes the indicator identity is trivial, and where it does not vanish the integrand must be nonzero somewhere, which yields $y\in\mathfrak{I}(p)$ with $K_{\mathfrak{s}(p)}(y,x)\neq0$; the scale-$\mathfrak{s}(p)$ kernel then gives $\operatorname{dist}(y,x)\le D^{\mathfrak{s}(p)}/2$ while the cube $\mathfrak{I}(p)$ sits in $B(\mathfrak{c}(p),4D^{\mathfrak{s}(p)})$, so $x$ is within $5D^{\mathfrak{s}(p)}$ of $\mathfrak{c}(p)$.

steps.explanation: Since $E(p)\subseteq\mathfrak{I}(p)$ (`E_subset_𝓘`), the lemma `adjoint_eq_adjoint_indicator` — which says that $E(p)\subseteq\mathfrak{I}(p')$ implies $T_p^*f=T_p^*(\mathbf{1}_{\mathfrak{I}(p')}f)$ — rewrites the left-hand side, so the claim becomes $T_p^*(\mathbf{1}_{\mathfrak{I}(p)}f)=\mathbf{1}_{B}\cdot T_p^*(\mathbf{1}_{\mathfrak{I}(p)}f)$ with $B=B(\mathfrak{c}(p),5D^{\mathfrak{s}(p)})$. Extensionality then reduces this function identity to the pointwise identity at an arbitrary $x\in X$.

Split on whether the value $g(x):=T_p^*(\mathbf{1}_{\mathfrak{I}(p)}f)(x)$ vanishes. In the vanishing case the pointwise identity $g(x)=\mathbf{1}_B(x)g(x)$ holds because a function that is zero at $x$ coincides there with any of its indicators (`Set.indicator_apply_eq_self`).

In the nonvanishing case, it suffices to prove $x\in B$: if $x$ lies in the set, the indicator at $x$ is $1$, so $\mathbf{1}_B(x)g(x)=g(x)$ (`Set.indicator_of_mem`), which is the goal up to symmetry. This is the only remaining point.

Produce a point $y\in\mathfrak{I}(p)$ with $K_{\mathfrak{s}(p)}(y,x)\neq0$, by contraposing against the nonvanishing of $g(x)$: assume $K_{\mathfrak{s}(p)}(y,x)=0$ for every $y\in\mathfrak{I}(p)$ and show the integral vanishes. For $y\in E(p)$, simplification of the integrand (conjugation is injective on zero, the exponential factor is never zero, and the indicator rewrites to the implication $y\in\mathfrak{I}(p)\Rightarrow f(y)=0$) reduces the vanishing of $\overline{K_{\mathfrak{s}(p)}(y,x)}\,e^{i(Q(y)(y)-Q(y)(x))}\,\mathbf{1}_{\mathfrak{I}(p)}f(y)$ to the disjunction '$K_{\mathfrak{s}(p)}(y,x)=0$ or ($y\in\mathfrak{I}(p)$ and $f(y)=0$)'; the left alternative holds because $y\in E(p)\subseteq\mathfrak{I}(p)$ (`E_subset_𝓘`) and the kernel vanishes there by hypothesis. Hence the integrand vanishes on all of $E(p)$ and the integral is zero (`setIntegral_eq_zero_of_forall_eq_zero`).

Show that this $y$ forces $x$ into the ball. Membership in $B$ is rewritten as $\operatorname{dist}(x,\mathfrak{c}(p))<5D^{\mathfrak{s}(p)}$, and one estimates $$\operatorname{dist}(x,\mathfrak{c}(p))\le\operatorname{dist}(y,x)+\operatorname{dist}(y,\mathfrak{c}(p))<D^{\mathfrak{s}(p)}/2+4D^{\mathfrak{s}(p)}.$$ The first term is bounded by the triangle inequality; the bound $\operatorname{dist}(y,x)\le D^{\mathfrak{s}(p)}/2$ comes from $K_{\mathfrak{s}(p)}(y,x)\neq0$ (`dist_mem_Icc_of_Ks_ne_zero`, which puts $\operatorname{dist}(y,x)$ in the interval $[D^{\mathfrak{s}(p)-1}/4,\,D^{\mathfrak{s}(p)}/2]$; only the upper end is used), and $\operatorname{dist}(y,\mathfrak{c}(p))<4D^{\mathfrak{s}(p)}$ from $y\in\mathfrak{I}(p)$ and the grid inclusion $\mathfrak{I}(p)\subseteq B(\mathfrak{c}(p),4D^{\mathfrak{s}(p)})$ (`GridStructure.Grid_subset_ball`). Finally $D^{\mathfrak{s}(p)}/2+4D^{\mathfrak{s}(p)}\le5D^{\mathfrak{s}(p)}$ follows by factoring out the common $D^{\mathfrak{s}(p)}$ and checking the numerical inequality $2^{-1}+4\le5$.

explanations.name: TileStructure.Forest.adjoint_tile_support2
explanations.statement: Let $X$ be a metric space carrying the data of the proof ($a\in\mathbb{N}$, $q\in\mathbb{R}$, $K:X\to X\to\mathbb{C}$, $\sigma_1,\sigma_2:X\to\mathbb{Z}$ and bounded measurable sets $F,G\subseteq X$, i.e. a `ProofData`), and let $\mathfrak{P}X$ be the tile structure with parameters $Q$, grid constant $D=2^{\mathfrak{c}a^2}$ (`defaultD a`), $\kappa=2^{-10a}$ (`defaultκ a`), $S$ (`defaultS X`) and base point `cancelPt X`. Let $t$ be a forest of tiles (a `TileStructure.Forest X n` for some $n\in\mathbb{N}$), let $u\in t$, and let $p\in\mathfrak{T}(u)$ lie in the tree attached to $u$. Then for every $f:X\to\mathbb{C}$ the adjoint Carleson operator $T_p^*$ satisfies $$T_p^*f=\mathbf{1}_{\mathfrak{I}(u)}\cdot T_p^*\bigl(\mathbf{1}_{\mathfrak{I}(u)}f\bigr),$$ that is, $T_p^*f$ is supported in $\mathfrak{I}(u)$ and $T_p^*$ only sees $f$ on $\mathfrak{I}(u)$.
explanations.summary: The operator $T_p^*$ integrates only over $E(p)$, and $E(p)\subseteq\mathfrak{I}(p)\subseteq\mathfrak{I}(u)$ because $p$ lies in the tree attached to $u$ in the forest, so $T_p^*$ applied to $f$ and to $\mathbf{1}_{\mathfrak{I}(u)}f$ agree. On the other hand `adjoint_tile_support1` locates the support of $T_p^*f$ in the ball $B(\mathfrak{c}(p),5D^{\mathfrak{s}(p)})$, and this ball lies in $\mathfrak{I}(u)$ by the forest nesting lemma, which places even the larger ball of radius $8D^{\mathfrak{s}(p)}$ inside $\mathfrak{I}(u)$. Hence the indicator of $\mathfrak{I}(u)$ is redundant on both sides, and the two displayed operators coincide.

steps.explanation: Rewrite the identity into the equivalent statement that the support ball of $p$ lies in $\mathfrak{I}(u)$, in four rewrites. First, the lemma `adjoint_eq_adjoint_indicator` — if $E(p)\subseteq\mathfrak{I}(p')$ then $T_p^*f=T_p^*(\mathbf{1}_{\mathfrak{I}(p')}f)$ — applied backwards with $p'=u$: the hypothesis $E(p)\subseteq\mathfrak{I}(u)$ is obtained by composing $E(p)\subseteq\mathfrak{I}(p)$ (`E_subset_𝓘`) with the set inclusion $\mathfrak{I}(p)\subseteq\mathfrak{I}(u)$ furnished by `smul_four_le`, which for $p\in\mathfrak{T}(u)$ gives $4\cdot p\le 1\cdot u$. This turns the right-hand side into $\mathbf{1}_{\mathfrak{I}(u)}\cdot T_p^*f$. Second, `adjoint_tile_support1`, which states $T_p^*f=\mathbf{1}_{B}T_p^*(\mathbf{1}_{\mathfrak{I}(p)}f)$ with $B=B(\mathfrak{c}(p),5D^{\mathfrak{s}(p)})$, is applied to both occurrences of $T_p^*f$, so both sides become indicators times $T_p^*(\mathbf{1}_{\mathfrak{I}(p)}f)$. Third, `indicator_indicator` combines the two indicators on the right into $\mathbf{1}_{\mathfrak{I}(u)\cap B}$. Fourth, the set-theoretic lemma `right_eq_inter`, used backwards — it identifies $\mathfrak{I}(u)\cap B$ with $B$ once $B\subseteq\mathfrak{I}(u)$ is known — makes the two sides identical and leaves the single remaining goal $B\subseteq\mathfrak{I}(u)$.

Prove $B(\mathfrak{c}(p),5D^{\mathfrak{s}(p)})\subseteq\mathfrak{I}(u)$. Since $D^{\mathfrak{s}(p)}>0$, the radius inequality $5D^{\mathfrak{s}(p)}\le 8D^{\mathfrak{s}(p)}$ holds, so `ball_subset_ball` gives $B(\mathfrak{c}(p),5D^{\mathfrak{s}(p)})\subseteq B(\mathfrak{c}(p),8D^{\mathfrak{s}(p)})$; `gcongr` reduces the radius inequality to $5\le 8$, which `norm_num` closes. The forest nesting lemma `t.ball_subset hu hp` gives $B(\mathfrak{c}(p),8D^{\mathfrak{s}(p)})\subseteq\mathfrak{I}(u)$, and transitivity yields the required inclusion.

notation.meaning: the open ball of radius $r$ about the point $x$
the tree of tiles attached to the tile $u$ in the forest

results.name: TileStructure.Forest.adjoint_tree_estimate + TileStructure.Forest.indicator_adjoint_tree_estimate
results.statement_reasoning: The candidate is Equivalent to the reference statement. Together, the two Lean declarations `adjoint_tree_estimate` and `indicator_adjoint_tree_estimate` establish the exact two $L^2$ bounds stated in the blueprint. Initial parameters and ambient hypotheses (such as the metric space ProofData, explicit tile-structure parameters where $\mathbb{c}=100$ recovers the exponents $181a^3$ and $282a^3$, extended-real norm conventions, and compact support in a proper space setting) are standard formalization conventions that do not alter the mathematical content.

reference_steps.step: Use the bilinear tree-density estimate and adjointness to bound $|\int_X \overline{\sum_{\mathfrak{p}\in\mathfrak{T}(\mathfrak{u})} T_{\mathfrak{p}}^* g}\, f \,\mathrm{d}\mu| \le 2^{181a^3} \mathrm{dens}_1(\mathfrak{T}(\mathfrak{u}))^{1/2} \|g\|_2 \|f\|_2$.
reference_steps.evidence: Part 1, Step 5: "Apply `adjoint_density_tree_bound1` with $f:=T^*_{\mathfrak{T}(u)}g$: it states that for bounded compactly supported $f,g$ with $\operatorname{supp}g\subseteq G$ and $u\in t$, $\|\int \overline{T^*_{\mathfrak{T}(u)}g}\,f\|_{\mathrm e}\le C_{7.3.1.1}(a)\,\mathrm{dens}_1(\mathfrak{T}(u))^{1/2}\|f\|_2\|g\|_2$."

reference_steps.step: Choose $f = \sum_{\mathfrak{p}\in\mathfrak{T}(\mathfrak{u})} T_{\mathfrak{p}}^* g$, observe that $f$ is bounded with bounded support so $\|f\|_2 < \infty$, and divide by $\|f\|_2$ to obtain the first bound.
reference_steps.evidence: Part 1, Steps 1–3: Splits on $\|T^*_{\mathfrak{T}(u)}g\|_{L^2}=0$, notes $T^*_{\mathfrak{T}(u)}g$ is bounded and compactly supported hence has finite $L^2$-norm, and multiplies the target inequality by $\|T^*_{\mathfrak{T}(u)}g\|_{L^2}$ using `ENNReal.mul_le_mul_iff_left`.

reference_steps.step: Prove the second bound analogously by setting $f = \mathbf{1}_F \sum_{\mathfrak{p}\in\mathfrak{T}(\mathfrak{u})} T_{\mathfrak{p}}^* g$ and applying the corresponding two-density bilinear bound.
reference_steps.evidence: Part 2, Steps 1–4: Sets $h:=1_F T^*_{\mathfrak{T}(u)}g$, verifies $0 < \|h\|_2 < \infty$ in the nontrivial case via bounded compact support, rewrites $h\overline{h} = \overline{T^*_{\mathfrak{T}(u)}g}\cdot h$ using $1_F\cdot 1_F = 1_F$, and applies `adjoint_density_tree_bound2` with $f=h$.

explanations.name: TileStructure.Forest.adjoint_tree_estimate
explanations.statement:
Let $X$ be a metric space carrying proof data $\mathrm{ProofData}(a,q,K,\sigma_1,\sigma_2,F,G)$ (in particular a doubling measure $\mathrm{vol}$, a kernel $K$, and the tile structure of the given constants), let $t$ be a forest of order $n$, let $u$ be a tile of $t$, and let $g:X\to\mathbb{C}$ be bounded and compactly supported with $\operatorname{supp} g\subseteq G$. Then the adjoint Carleson sum over the tree $\mathfrak{T}(u)$ satisfies
$$\|T^*_{\mathfrak{T}(u)}g\|_{L^2(\mathrm{vol})}\;\le\; C_{7.3.1.1}(a)\,\mathrm{dens}_1\big(\mathfrak{T}(u)\big)^{1/2}\,\|g\|_{L^2(\mathrm{vol})},$$
where $C_{7.3.1.1}(a)=2^{(\mathbb{c}+6+\mathbb{c}/2+\mathbb{c}/4)a^{3}}\in\mathbb{R}_{\ge0}$ ($\mathbb{c}$ the grid constant of $D=2^{\mathbb{c}a^{2}}$; the blueprint value is $2^{181a^{3}}$), and $\mathrm{dens}_1$ is the $\mathbb{R}_{\ge0}^{\infty}$-valued density of a set $\mathfrak{P}'$ of tiles,
$$\mathrm{dens}_1(\mathfrak{P}')=\sup_{p'\in\mathfrak{P}'}\ \sup_{l\ge 2}\ l^{-a}\sup\Big\{\tfrac{|E_2(l,p)|}{|\mathfrak{I}(p)|}\;:\;p\in\mathrm{lowerCubes}(\mathfrak{P}'),\ \mathrm{smul}_l(p')\le \mathrm{smul}_l(p)\Big\},$$
with the exponent $1/2$ interpreted as the real power $2^{-1}$ in $\mathbb{R}_{\ge0}^{\infty}$, the whole inequality being an inequality of extended nonnegative reals (the constant $C_{7.3.1.1}(a)$ is the nonnegative real coerced into $\mathbb{R}_{\ge0}^{\infty}$).
explanations.summary: The proof reduces the $L^2$ bound for the adjoint Carleson sum to the bilinear estimate `adjoint_density_tree_bound1`. If the sum vanishes there is nothing to prove; otherwise one multiplies the desired inequality by the finite nonzero norm $\|T^*_{\mathfrak{T}(u)}g\|_2$, turns the square of that norm into the extended norm of $\int T^*g\,\overline{T^*g}$, and merely reorders the pointwise factors and the scalar product so that the goal matches the bilinear estimate, whose two function arguments are $T^*_{\mathfrak{T}(u)}g$ (bounded compactly supported by the corresponding closure property) and $g$.

steps.explanation: Split on whether $\|T^*_{\mathfrak{T}(u)}g\|_{L^2}=0$. In the vanishing case the left side is $0$ and the right side is a product of nonnegative extended reals, so the inequality is immediate.

Record for later use that $T^*_{\mathfrak{T}(u)}g$ is again bounded and compactly supported, because $g$ is (`BoundedCompactSupport.adjointCarlesonSum`); this will supply the $L^2$-membership (`BoundedCompactSupport.memLp`) and hence the finiteness of its $L^2$-norm.

In the nonvanishing case, multiply both sides of the inequality by the (nonzero, finite) norm $\|T^*_{\mathfrak{T}(u)}g\|_{L^2}$, using `ENNReal.mul_le_mul_iff_left` in its reverse direction (the facts that this norm is nonzero and not $\infty$ are exactly the two side conditions). Rewrite the resulting factor $\|T^*g\|_2\cdot\|T^*g\|_2$ as $\|T^*g\|_2^2$, then replace that square by the extended norm of the integral $\int T^*g\,\overline{T^*g}$ via `eLpNorm_two_eq_enorm_integral_mul_conj`; finally reassociate and commute the factors on the right. The goal becomes $\|\int T^*g\,\overline{T^*g}\|_{\mathrm e}\le C_{7.3.1.1}(a)\,\mathrm{dens}_1(\mathfrak{T}(u))^{1/2}\,\|T^*g\|_2\,\|g\|_2$.

Inside the integral, swap the two pointwise factors, replacing $T^*g\cdot\overline{T^*g}$ by $\overline{T^*g}\cdot T^*g$, so that the integrand has the shape required by the estimate about to be applied.

Apply `adjoint_density_tree_bound1` with $f:=T^*_{\mathfrak{T}(u)}g$: it states that for bounded compactly supported $f,g$ with $\operatorname{supp}g\subseteq G$ and $u\in t$, $\|\int \overline{T^*_{\mathfrak{T}(u)}g}\,f\|_{\mathrm e}\le C_{7.3.1.1}(a)\,\mathrm{dens}_1(\mathfrak{T}(u))^{1/2}\|f\|_2\|g\|_2$. With $f$ the adjoint sum, this is precisely the goal.

the density of a set of tiles, valued in $\mathbb{R}_{\ge0}^{\infty}$, with the formula given in the statement
the constant $2^{(\mathbb{c}+6+\mathbb{c}/2+\mathbb{c}/4)a^{3}}$
the extended norm of the complex number or integral $z$, valued in $\mathbb{R}_{\ge0}^{\infty}$

explanations.name: TileStructure.Forest.indicator_adjoint_tree_estimate
explanations.statement:
Let $X$ be a metric space carrying proof data $(a,q,K,\sigma_1,\sigma_2,F,G)$ — so $q\in(1,2]$, $F$ and $G$ are bounded measurable sets, $X$ is equipped with the associated doubling measure, and the linearised nontangential operators have bounded strong type $(2,2)$ with constant $C_{T_s}(a)$ — together with a tile structure whose constants are $D=2^{\mathbb{c}a^2}$, $\kappa=2^{-10a}$, a scale bound $S$ and cancellation point $o$. Let $t$ be a forest of depth $n$, let $u$ be a tile with $u\in t$, and let $g:X\to\mathbb{C}$ be bounded with compact support and $\operatorname{supp}g\subseteq G$. Write $\mathfrak{T}(u)$ for the tree of tiles attached to $u$ in the forest and $T^*_{\mathfrak{C}}g=\sum_{p\in\mathfrak{C}}T_p^*g$ for the adjoint Carleson sum over a set $\mathfrak{C}$ of tiles. Then
$$\big\|1_F\,T^*_{\mathfrak{T}(u)}g\big\|_2\;\le\;C_{7.3.1.2}(a)\;\mathrm{dens}_1(\mathfrak{T}(u))^{1/2}\,\mathrm{dens}_2(\mathfrak{T}(u))^{1/2}\,\|g\|_2,$$
where $C_{7.3.1.2}(a)=2^{(2\mathbb{c}+7+\mathbb{c}/2+\mathbb{c}/4)a^3}$ (value $2^{282a^3}$ in the blueprint), the norms are $L^2$ extended norms over $X$, and the densities are valued in $\mathbb{R}_{\ge0}^{\infty}$ with $\mathrm{dens}_2(\mathfrak{P}')=\sup_{p\in\mathfrak{P}'}\sup_{r\ge 4D^{\mathfrak{s}(p)}}\frac{|F\cap B(\mathfrak{c}(p),r)|}{|B(\mathfrak{c}(p),r)|}$ and $\mathrm{dens}_1(\mathfrak{P}')=\sup_{p'\in\mathfrak{P}'}\sup_{l\ge2} l^{-a}\sup_{p\in\mathrm{lowerCubes}(\mathfrak{P}'),\,lp'\le lp}\frac{|E_2(lp)|}{|\mathfrak{I}(p)|}$.
explanations.summary: The proof disposes of the degenerate case $\|1_FT^*_{\mathfrak{T}(u)}g\|_2=0$ first. Otherwise it multiplies the desired inequality by the finite, nonzero quantity $\|h\|_2$ with $h=1_FT^*_{\mathfrak{T}(u)}g$, writes $\|h\|_2^2$ as the extended norm of $\int h\overline h$, and reduces the claim to the single bilinear estimate $\|\int \overline{T^*_{\mathfrak{T}(u)}g}\,h\|_{\mathrm e}\le C_{7.3.1.2}(a)\,\mathrm{dens}_1^{1/2}\mathrm{dens}_2^{1/2}\|h\|_2\|g\|_2$. The identification of the integrands is a pointwise computation using that $1_F$ is a real-valued indicator: $h\overline h=\overline{T^*g}\,h$. The bilinear estimate is then applied with the admissible input $f=h$, whose support lies in $F$.

steps.explanation: Split on whether $h:=1_F T^*_{\mathfrak{T}(u)}g$ has vanishing $L^2$ norm. If $\|h\|_2=0$, the left-hand side of the claim is $0$ and the right-hand side is a product of nonnegative extended reals, so the inequality holds trivially.

Now assume $\|h\|_2\neq0$. First record that $h$ is bounded with compact support: $T^*_{\mathfrak{T}(u)}g$ is, being an adjoint Carleson sum of a bounded compactly supported $g$ (`MeasureTheory.BoundedCompactSupport.adjointCarlesonSum`), and multiplying by the indicator of the measurable set $F$ preserves this (`MeasureTheory.BoundedCompactSupport.indicator`, using measurability of $F$ from the proof data). Hence $h\in L^2$, so $\|h\|_2\neq\infty$, and one may multiply the inequality by $\|h\|_2$ on both sides, which is legitimate precisely because $0<\|h\|_2<\infty$ (`ENNReal.mul_le_mul_iff_left`). The goal becomes $\|h\|_2^2\le C_{7.3.1.2}(a)\,\mathrm{dens}_1^{1/2}\mathrm{dens}_2^{1/2}\|h\|_2\|g\|_2$; the square $\|h\|_2^2$ is then rewritten as $\|\int h\,\overline{h}\|_{\mathrm e}$ by the $L^2$ identity `MeasureTheory.eLpNorm_two_eq_enorm_integral_mul_conj`, and the right-hand side is reassociated so that the two $L^2$ norms sit together.

The calculation begins by identifying the integrand pointwise: $h(x)\,\overline{h(x)} = \overline{T^*_{\mathfrak{T}(u)}g(x)}\cdot h(x)$. Explicitly, Lean rewrites the occurrence of $h(x)$ inside the conjugate as $1_F(x)\,T^*g(x)$; conjugation is then pushed through the product, the conjugate of the indicator $1_F$ is $1_F$ itself (it is real-valued and $\overline{1}=1$), the factor $1_F(x)$ is reassociated and commuted so that it stands next to $h(x)$, the product $1_F(x)\cdot h(x)$ is collapsed back to $h(x)$ using $1_F(x)\cdot1_F(x)=1_F(x)$, and the last step is plain commutativity. This turns the left-hand side into $\|\int \overline{T^*_{\mathfrak{T}(u)}g}\cdot h\|_{\mathrm e}$.

Apply the bilinear tree estimate `TileStructure.Forest.adjoint_density_tree_bound2` with $f=h$: it requires $f$ bounded with compact support with support in $F$ (satisfied, since $h$ is $1_F$ times something), $g$ bounded with compact support supported in $G$, and $u\in t$, and it concludes exactly $\|\int \overline{T^*_{\mathfrak{T}(u)}g}\,f\|_{\mathrm e}\le C_{7.3.1.2}(a)\,\mathrm{dens}_1(\mathfrak{T}(u))^{1/2}\mathrm{dens}_2(\mathfrak{T}(u))^{1/2}\|f\|_2\|g\|_2$, which is the current goal.

notation.meaning: the constant $2^{(2\mathbb{c}+7+\mathbb{c}/2+\mathbb{c}/4)a^3}$ of the tree density estimates ($2^{282a^3}$ in the blueprint)

results.name: TileStructure.Forest.adjoint_tree_control
results.statement_reasoning: The candidate statement matches the reference statement after accounting for standard formalization conventions in the Carleson project: ambient metric/measure-theoretic proof data (which supplies parameters like $a \ge 4$ and bounded measurable $G$), representing $\mathfrak{u} \in \mathfrak{U}$ as a tile $u$ in a forest $t$, requiring `BoundedCompactSupport` (standard for bounded functions supported on the bounded set $G$ in a proper space, plus measurability), and writing the constant as $C_{7.4.3}(a) = 2^{(\mathbb{c} + 7 + \mathbb{c}/2 + \mathbb{c}/4)a^3}$, which equals $2^{182a^3}$ for the blueprint's grid constant $\mathbb{c} = 100$.

reference_steps.step: Apply Minkowski's inequality ($L^2$ triangle inequality) to split $S_{2,\mathfrak{u}}g$ into its constituent terms, bound them respectively via the adjoint tree estimate and the Hardy-Littlewood maximal inequality (along with the trivial $L^2$ bound on $g$), and combine the constants using $a \ge 4$.
reference_steps.evidence: Steps 1–2 apply the $L^2$ triangle inequality (`eLpNorm_add_le`) twice to split $S_{2,\mathfrak{u}}f = \|T^*_{\mathfrak{T}(u)}f\|_{\mathrm{e}} + M_{\mathfrak{B}}f + \|f\|_{\mathrm{e}}$; Step 3 bounds the three pieces using `adjoint_tree_estimate`, `hasStrongType_maximalFunction_one`, and `eLpNorm_enorm`; Steps 4–5 bound the density by $1$ (`dens₁_le_one`) and conclude $C_{7.3.1.1}(a) + CMB(2^a,2) + 1 \le C_{7.4.3}(a)$ via `le_C7_4_3` using $a \ge 4$ (`four_le_a`).

explanations.name: TileStructure.Forest.adjoint_tree_control
explanations.statement:
Let $X$ be a metric space carrying proof data $(a,q,K,\sigma_1,\sigma_2,F,G)$ (so $a\ge 4$, $q\in(1,2]$, $F,G$ bounded measurable, and $\mathrm{vol}$ is a doubling measure with the associated tile structure of constants $D=2^{\mathbb c a^2}$, $\kappa=2^{-10a}$, $S$ and cancellation point $o$). Let $t$ be a forest of order $n$, let $u$ be a tile with $u\in t$, and let $f:X\to\mathbb{C}$ be bounded and compactly supported with $\operatorname{supp}f\subseteq G$. Then the adjoint boundary operator $S_{2,\mathfrak u}f=\|T^*_{\mathfrak T(u)}f\|_{\mathrm e}+M_{\mathfrak B}f+\|f\|_{\mathrm e}$ satisfies, in $\mathbb{R}_{\ge0}^{\infty}$,
$$\|S_{2,\mathfrak u}f\|_{L^2(\mathrm{vol})}\;\le\;C_{7.4.3}(a)\,\|f\|_{L^2(\mathrm{vol})},$$
where $C_{7.4.3}(a)=2^{(\mathbb c+7+\mathbb c/2+\mathbb c/4)a^3}\in\mathbb{R}_{\ge0}$ ($2^{182a^3}$ in the blueprint, $\mathbb c$ the grid constant).
explanations.summary: The proof is a three-term splitting followed by a constant bookkeeping. The boundary operator is the sum of the adjoint Carleson sum over the tree, the uncentered maximal function over the ball family $\mathfrak B$, and $|f|$ itself; two applications of the $L^2$ triangle inequality separate them. Each term is then controlled by $\|f\|_2$: the adjoint tree estimate gives $C_{7.3.1.1}(a)\,\mathrm{dens}_1(\mathfrak T(u))^{1/2}\|f\|_2$, the strong $(2,2)$ bound for the maximal function gives $CMB(2^a,2)\|f\|_2$, and the $|f|$ term is dominated by $\|f\|_2$ since the extended norm has the same $L^2$ norm as $f$. Since a density is at most $1$, the coefficient is at most $C_{7.3.1.1}(a)+CMB(2^a,2)+1$, which the numerical lemma `le_C7_4_3` (using $a\ge4$) places below $C_{7.4.3}(a)$.

steps.explanation: Unfold the boundary operator, which by definition is the extended-nonnegative-real function $\|T^*_{\mathfrak T(u)}f(x)\|_{\mathrm e}+M_{\mathfrak B}f(x)+\|f(x)\|_{\mathrm e}$, and peel off its last summand: the triangle inequality for the $L^2$ norm, `eLpNorm_add_le` with $1\le 2$, bounds the $L^2$ norm of the whole operator by the $L^2$ norm of $\|T^*_{\mathfrak T(u)}f\|_{\mathrm e}+M_{\mathfrak B}f$ plus the $L^2$ norm of $\|f\|_{\mathrm e}$.

Apply the same triangle inequality `eLpNorm_add_le` once more to split the remaining sum into the two $L^2$ norms $\|\,\|T^*_{\mathfrak T(u)}f\|_{\mathrm e}\|_2$ and $\|M_{\mathfrak B}f\|_2$; `gcongr` matches the common third summand $eLpNorm(\|f\|_{\mathrm e})$ on both sides and leaves exactly that triangle inequality as the only goal.

Bound the three summands separately against $\|f\|_2$, as three goals produced by `gcongr`. (i) Since $f$ is a.e. strongly measurable (bounded compact support gives this), hence so is its adjoint Carleson sum, `eLpNorm_enorm` replaces $\|\,\|T^*_{\mathfrak T(u)}f\|_{\mathrm e}\|_2$ by $\|T^*_{\mathfrak T(u)}f\|_2$, and the adjoint tree estimate `adjoint_tree_estimate` — which states $\|T^*_{\mathfrak T(u)}g\|_2\le C_{7.3.1.1}(a)\,\mathrm{dens}_1(\mathfrak T(u))^{1/2}\|g\|_2$ for bounded compactly supported $g$ with $\operatorname{supp}g\subseteq G$ — gives the bound $C_{7.3.1.1}(a)\,\mathrm{dens}_1(\mathfrak T(u))^{1/2}\|f\|_2$. (ii) The maximal function has strong type $(2,2)$ with constant $CMB(A,2)$ (`hasStrongType_maximalFunction_one`, applied with $p=2>1$ and $A=\mathrm{defaultA}(a)=2^a$), and $f\in L^2$ because it is bounded and compactly supported (`MeasureTheory.BoundedCompactSupport.memLp`), giving $\|M_{\mathfrak B}f\|_2\le CMB(2^a,2)\|f\|_2$. (iii) Since $f$ is a.e. strongly measurable, `eLpNorm_enorm` identifies $\|\,\|f\|_{\mathrm e}\|_2$ with $\|f\|_2$, and the required inequality $\|\,\|f\|_{\mathrm e}\|_2\le\|f\|_2$ follows. This yields the bound $C_{7.3.1.1}(a)\,\mathrm{dens}_1(\mathfrak T(u))^{1/2}\|f\|_2+CMB(2^a,2)\|f\|_2+\|f\|_2$.

Replace the density factor by $1$: the density of any set of tiles is at most $1$ (`dens₁_le_one`, i.e. $\mathrm{dens}_1\mathfrak P'\le 1$), and `gcongr` reduces the claim to that single inequality after the right-hand side is expanded as a sum of three products (`add_mul`, `one_mul`). The result is the bound $(C_{7.3.1.1}(a)\cdot 1^{1/2}+CMB(2^a,2)+1)\|f\|_2$.

Compare constants: `gcongr` cancels the common nonnegative factor $\|f\|_2$, leaving the numerical inequality $C_{7.3.1.1}(a)\cdot 1^{1/2}+CMB(2^a,2)+1\le C_{7.4.3}(a)$; after simplifying $1^{1/2}=1$ and the cast of $\mathrm{defaultA}(a)=2^a$ and normalising the coercions with `norm_cast`, this is exactly `le_C7_4_3`, the numerical estimate $C_{7.3.1.1}(a)+CMB(2^a,2)+1\le C_{7.4.3}(a)$ valid for $a\ge4$ (which holds by `four_le_a`).

notation.meaning: the adjoint boundary operator $\|T^*_{\mathfrak T(u)}f\|_{\mathrm e}+M_{\mathfrak B}f+\|f\|_{\mathrm e}$
the uncentered Hardy–Littlewood maximal function over the ball family $\mathfrak B$, $\sup_{i\in\mathfrak B}1_{B(c_i,r_i)}(x)(\fint_{B(c_i,r_i)}|f|^p)^{1/p}$, here at $p=1$
the constant $2^{(\mathbb c+7+\mathbb c/2+\mathbb c/4)a^3}$, i.e. $2^{182a^3}$ in the blueprint
the index set $\{0,\dots,S+5\}\times\{0,\dots,2S+3\}\times\mathrm{Grid}$ of the maximal function $M_{\mathfrak B}$

results.name: TileStructure.Forest.𝔗_subset_𝔖₀ + TileStructure.Forest.overlap_implies_distance
results.statement_reasoning: The reference statement has two assertions for distinct tiles u_1, u_2 in a forest with I(u_1) subset I(u_2): (1) any tile p in T(u_1) cup T(u_2) whose cube I(p) intersects I(u_1) belongs to S, and (2) in particular T(u_1) subset S. From the reference proof, membership of p in T(u_1) cup T(u_2) in S is defined by the distance bound d_p(Q(u_1), Q(u_2)) >= 2^{Zn/2} with Z = 2^{12a}. In the candidate, Part 2 (`TileStructure.Forest.overlap_implies_distance`) states assertion (1) and Part 1 (`TileStructure.Forest.𝔗_subset_𝔖₀`) states assertion (2), carrying the explicit Chapter 7 tile-structure parameters and defining S_0(t, u_1, u_2) by the exact same condition. Accounting for formalization conventions and notation (dyadic cube order <= for inclusion, non-disjointness for non-empty intersection), the combined candidate statement makes the exact same mathematical claim.

reference_steps.step: For p in T(u_1), use I(p) subset I(u_1) subset I(u_2), the reverse triangle inequality, the forest separation bound (>= 2^{Z(n+1)}), the tree frequency-ball bound (<= 4), and Z = 2^{12a} >= 4 to obtain d_p(Q(u_1), Q(u_2)) >= 2^{Z(n+1)} - 4 >= 2^{Zn/2}, giving p in S (and T(u_1) subset S).
reference_steps.evidence: Part 2 (`overlap_implies_distance`), Steps 3 and 4 establish 2^{Z(n+1)} - 4 >= 2^{Zn/2} from 4 <= Z and apply the triangle inequality, `TileStructure.Forest.lt_dist'` (using I(p) <= I(u_1) <= I(u_2)), and `TileStructure.Forest.smul_four_le` (giving ball inclusion of radius 4) when p in T(u_1). Part 1 (`𝔗_subset_𝔖₀`), Steps 1 and 2 deduce T(u_1) subset S_0 by showing every p in T(u_1) has nonempty cube contained in I(u_1), hence meeting I(u_1).

reference_steps.step: For p in T(u_2) with I(p) subset I(u_1), apply the symmetric argument with u_1 and u_2 swapped to conclude p in S.
reference_steps.evidence: Part 2 (`overlap_implies_distance`), Step 5 handles p in T(u_2) under the reduced hypothesis I(p) <= I(u_1) as the mirror image of Step 4, applying the triangle inequality, `TileStructure.Forest.lt_dist'` with (u, u') = (u_1, u_2), and `TileStructure.Forest.smul_four_le` for u_2.

reference_steps.step: When I(p) is not contained in I(u_1) (with I(p) cap I(u_1) nonempty), use the dyadic property to get I(u_1) subset I(p), pick p' in T(u_1) so that I(p') subset I(u_1) subset I(p), and apply monotonicity of cube metrics together with the bound at p' to conclude p in S.
reference_steps.evidence: Part 2 (`overlap_implies_distance`), Step 2 performs this reduction via `wlog`: when I(p) is not <= I(u_1), non-disjointness and `le_or_ge_or_disjoint` yield I(u_1) <= I(p); it chooses p' in T(u_1) via `Forest.nonempty`, notes I(p') <= I(u_1) <= I(p), applies the I(p') <= I(u_1) case to p' (yielding >= 2^{Zn/2}), and transfers the lower bound to p via `Grid.dist_mono`.

explanations.name: TileStructure.Forest.𝔗_subset_𝔖₀
explanations.statement: Let $X$ be a metric space carrying the standing Chapter 7 proof data: a doubling measure of constant $2^a$, a parameter $q\in(1,2]$, a kernel $K$, measurable exponents $\sigma_1\le\sigma_2$ with finite ranges, bounded measurable sets $F,G$, and the associated simple function $Q:X\to\Theta(X)$ with the bounded strong type property for the linearized nontangential operator. Equip $X$ with a tile structure subordinate to $Q$ with $D=2^{\mathbb{c}a^2}$, $\kappa=2^{-10a}$, depth constant $S$ and base point $o$ (a point at which every $\Theta(X)$-function vanishes), so that tiles $p$ carry a dyadic cube $\mathfrak{I}(p)$, a value $\mathcal{Q}p$ and a tree $\mathfrak{T}(p)$. Let $t$ be a forest of depth $n$ and let $u_1,u_2\in t$ be distinct tiles with $\mathfrak{I}(u_1)\le\mathfrak{I}(u_2)$. Then $\mathfrak{T}(u_1)$ is contained in $\mathfrak{S}_0(t,u_1,u_2)=\{p\in\mathfrak{T}(u_1)\cup\mathfrak{T}(u_2):2^{Zn/2}\le\mathrm{dist}_{(p)}(\mathcal{Q}u_1,\mathcal{Q}u_2)\}$, where $Z=2^{12a}$.
explanations.summary: For each tile $p$ in the tree of $u_1$, the proof invokes the overlap-distance lemma, which reduces the claim to showing that the cube of $p$ meets the cube of $u_1$. Nonemptiness of grid cubes provides a point of $p$'s cube, and the forest inequality $\mathrm{smul}(4,p)\le\mathrm{smul}(1,u_1)$ places that same point in $u_1$'s cube. Hence the cubes meet, and the overlap-distance lemma gives $p\in\mathfrak{S}_0(t,u_1,u_2)$.

steps.explanation: The inclusion is proved pointwise: fix a tile $p$ with $p\in\mathfrak{T}(u_1)$, so that $p$ also lies in $\mathfrak{T}(u_1)\cup\mathfrak{T}(u_2)$, and the goal is $p\in\mathfrak{S}_0(t,u_1,u_2)$. Apply `TileStructure.Forest.overlap_implies_distance`, which states that for distinct $u_1,u_2\in t$ with $\mathfrak{I}(u_1)\le\mathfrak{I}(u_2)$, every $p\in\mathfrak{T}(u_1)\cup\mathfrak{T}(u_2)$ whose cube $\mathfrak{I}(p)$ is not disjoint from $\mathfrak{I}(u_1)$ lies in $\mathfrak{S}_0(t,u_1,u_2)$. Applied to the membership of $u_1,u_2$ in $t$, the distinctness $u_1\ne u_2$, the order $\mathfrak{I}(u_1)\le\mathfrak{I}(u_2)$ and the union membership of $p$, it leaves exactly the goal of showing that $\mathfrak{I}(p)$ and $\mathfrak{I}(u_1)$ are not disjoint.

Grid cubes are nonempty (`Grid.nonempty`), so choose a point $c\in\mathfrak{I}(p)$ (here $\mathfrak{I}(p)$ is viewed as a subset of $X$). From `TileStructure.Forest.smul_four_le`, applied to $u_1\in t$ and $p\in\mathfrak{T}(u_1)$, the tile comparison $\mathrm{smul}(4,p)\le\mathrm{smul}(1,u_1)$ holds; its first component compares the cubes, and applied to $c$ it gives $c\in\mathfrak{I}(u_1)$. Thus $c$ is a common point of $\mathfrak{I}(p)$ and $\mathfrak{I}(u_1)$, so the two cubes are not disjoint. This discharges the remaining goal and yields $p\in\mathfrak{S}_0(t,u_1,u_2)$.

notation.meaning: the pair consisting of the dyadic cube $\mathfrak{I}(p)$ and the ball of radius $l$ about $\mathcal{Q}p$ in the function-distance metric attached to $p$

explanations.name: TileStructure.Forest.overlap_implies_distance
explanations.statement: Let $X$ be a metric space carrying the standing Chapter 7 proof data (parameters $a$ and $q\in(1,2]$, kernel $K$, exponents $\sigma_1\le\sigma_2$, sets $F,G$) and let $Q$ be a simple function on $X$ with values in $\Theta(X)$. Let the space be equipped with a tile structure subordinate to $Q$, with $D=2^{\mathbb{c}a^2}$, $\kappa=2^{-10a}$, depth constant $S$ and base point $o$, whose tiles $p$ carry a dyadic cube $\mathfrak{I}(p)$, a value $\mathcal{Q}p$ in $\Theta(X)$ and a scale $\mathfrak{s}(p)$. Let $t$ be a forest of depth $n$ and let $u_1,u_2\in t$ be distinct tiles with $\mathfrak{I}(u_1)\le\mathfrak{I}(u_2)$. If $p\in\mathfrak{T}(u_1)\cup\mathfrak{T}(u_2)$ and $\mathfrak{I}(p)$ is not disjoint from $\mathfrak{I}(u_1)$, then $p\in\mathfrak{S}_0(t,u_1,u_2)$, i.e. $2^{Zn/2}\le \mathrm{dist}_{(p)}(\mathcal{Q}u_1,\mathcal{Q}u_2)$, where $Z=2^{12a}$ and $\mathfrak{S}_0(t,u_1,u_2)=\{p\in\mathfrak{T}(u_1)\cup\mathfrak{T}(u_2): 2^{Zn/2}\le \mathrm{dist}_{(p)}(\mathcal{Q}u_1,\mathcal{Q}u_2)\}$.
explanations.summary: The proof shows that tiles $p$ lying over one of two distinct tiles $u_1,u_2$ of a forest whose cube meets $\mathfrak{I}(u_1)$ have $Q$-values that are far apart at the scale of $p$. By the trichotomy of grid cubes one first reduces to the case $\mathfrak{I}(p)\le\mathfrak{I}(u_1)$: if instead $\mathfrak{I}(u_1)\le\mathfrak{I}(p)$, one moves to a tile $p'$ over $u_1$ with $\mathfrak{I}(p')\le\mathfrak{I}(u_1)$, applies the statement there, and transfers the estimate back to $p$ by monotonicity of the function distance in the cube. In the reduced case the two alternatives $p\in\mathfrak{T}(u_1)$ and $p\in\mathfrak{T}(u_2)$ are handled symmetrically: the reverse triangle inequality splits $\mathrm{dist}_{(p)}(\mathcal{Q}u_1,\mathcal{Q}u_2)$ into a distance from $\mathcal{Q}p$ to the $Q$-value of the tile over which $p$ does *not* lie, which is $>2^{Z(n+1)}$ by the forest's separation property, minus the distance from $\mathcal{Q}p$ to the $Q$-value of the tile it does lie over, which is $\le 4$ because `smul_four_le` puts the radius-$1$ ball around the latter $Q$-value inside the radius-$4$ ball around $\mathcal{Q}p$. A purely numerical estimate $2^{Z(n+1)}-4\ge 2^{Zn/2}$, obtained from $Z\ge 4$, then yields the required lower bound $2^{Zn/2}$.

steps.explanation: Unfold the definition of $\mathfrak{S}_0$ and discharge its first membership condition with the hypothesis $hp$. Since $p$ is already known to lie in $\mathfrak{T}(u_1)\cup\mathfrak{T}(u_2)$, the goal becomes exactly the distance bound $2^{Zn/2}\le \mathrm{dist}_{(p)}(\mathcal{Q}u_1,\mathcal{Q}u_2)$.

Reduce by symmetry to the case $\mathfrak{I}(p)\le\mathfrak{I}(u_1)$ (a `wlog` argument, generalized over $p$; in the complementary case the goal is the same inequality, with the wlog hypothesis available as `this` for every tile satisfying the hypotheses and having its cube below $\mathfrak{I}(u_1)$). In the complementary case $\mathfrak{I}(p)\not\le\mathfrak{I}(u_1)$ together with non-disjointness of $\mathfrak{I}(p)$ and $\mathfrak{I}(u_1)$ gives $\mathfrak{I}(u_1)\le\mathfrak{I}(p)$, by the trichotomy `le_or_ge_or_disjoint` (for any two cubes $i,j$ one has $i\le j$ or $j\le i$ or they are disjoint). Choose $p'\in\mathfrak{T}(u_1)$, which exists by `TileStructure.Forest.nonempty`; from `TileStructure.Forest.smul_four_le` applied to $u_1$ and $p'$ get $\mathfrak{I}(p')\le\mathfrak{I}(u_1)$, so $\mathfrak{I}(p')$ meets $\mathfrak{I}(u_1)$ — witnessed by a point $c\in\mathfrak{I}(p')$ (which also lies in $\mathfrak{I}(u_1)$). Apply `this` to $p'$ to obtain the bound at $p'$, and transfer it to $p$ by monotonicity of the function distance under cube inclusion, `Grid.dist_mono` (if $I\le J$ then $\mathrm{dist}_{(I)}\le\mathrm{dist}_{(J)}$ for all $f,g$), applied to $\mathfrak{I}(p')\le\mathfrak{I}(u_1)\le\mathfrak{I}(p)$.

Establish the numerical inequality $2^{Z(n+1)}-4\ge 2^{Zn/2}$ for real powers of $2$. From `four_le_Z` ($4\le Z$) one gets $4\le Z(n+1)$, then $4\le 2^{Z(n+1)-1}$ because $2\le Z(n+1)-1$. Hence $2^{Z(n+1)}-4\ge 2^{Z(n+1)}-2^{Z(n+1)-1}=2^{Z(n+1)-1}\ge 2^{Zn}$ (monotonicity of $x\mapsto 2^x$ in the exponent, $Zn\le Z(n+1)-1$), and finally $2^{Zn}\ge 2^{Zn/2}$ by monotonicity of real powers with base $2\ge 1$ together with $Zn/2\le Zn$.

Split according to whether $p\in\mathfrak{T}(u_1)$ or $p\in\mathfrak{T}(u_2)$. In the first case, the triangle inequality in the pseudo-metric on $\Theta(X)$ attached to $p$ gives $\mathrm{dist}_{(p)}(\mathcal{Q}u_1,\mathcal{Q}u_2)\ge \mathrm{dist}_{(p)}(\mathcal{Q}p,\mathcal{Q}u_2)-\mathrm{dist}_{(p)}(\mathcal{Q}p,\mathcal{Q}u_1)$. The first term is $>2^{Z(n+1)}$ by `TileStructure.Forest.lt_dist'` (for distinct $u,u'\in t$, $p\in\mathfrak{T}(u')$ and $\mathfrak{I}(p)\le\mathfrak{I}(u)$, one has $2^{Z(n+1)}<\mathrm{dist}_{(p)}(\mathcal{Q}p,\mathcal{Q}u)$) applied with $(u,u')=(u_2,u_1)$, using $\mathfrak{I}(p)\le\mathfrak{I}(u_1)\le\mathfrak{I}(u_2)$. The second term is $\le 4$, because `TileStructure.Forest.smul_four_le` for $u_1$ supplies the ball inclusion $\mathrm{ball}_{(u_1)}(\mathcal{Q}u_1,1)\subseteq \mathrm{ball}_{(p)}(\mathcal{Q}p,4)$, and $\mathcal{Q}u_1\in\mathrm{ball}_{(u_1)}(\mathcal{Q}u_1,1)$; membership in $\mathrm{ball}_{(p)}(\mathcal{Q}p,4)$ gives the distance bound. So the difference is at least $2^{Z(n+1)}-4\ge 2^{Zn/2}$ by the preceding numerical inequality.

The second case, $p\in\mathfrak{T}(u_2)$, is the mirror image: $\mathrm{dist}_{(p)}(\mathcal{Q}u_1,\mathcal{Q}u_2)\ge \mathrm{dist}_{(p)}(\mathcal{Q}p,\mathcal{Q}u_1)-\mathrm{dist}_{(p)}(\mathcal{Q}p,\mathcal{Q}u_2)$ by the triangle inequality (`dist_triangle_right`), the first term is $>2^{Z(n+1)}$ by `TileStructure.Forest.lt_dist'` applied with $(u,u')=(u_1,u_2)$ and the hypothesis $\mathfrak{I}(p)\le\mathfrak{I}(u_1)$, and the second is $\le 4$ since `TileStructure.Forest.smul_four_le` for $u_2$ supplies $\mathrm{ball}_{(u_2)}(\mathcal{Q}u_2,1)\subseteq\mathrm{ball}_{(p)}(\mathcal{Q}p,4)$ and $\mathcal{Q}u_2$ lies in the former. Again the difference is at least $2^{Z(n+1)}-4\ge 2^{Zn/2}$.
